summary: cfgzen ships a Windows PE dropper executed on import that contacts files.catbox.moe
details: On `import dotcfg`, the top-level `dotcfg/__init__.py` unconditionally calls `_native.platform_check()`, handing execution to a shipped Windows PE (`_native.pyd`). The binary contains a WinHTTP client and raw socket imports (ws2_32.dll), enumerates host identifiers (COMPUTERNAME, HOSTNAME, USERNAME, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP) and a broad list of CI/sandbox indicators (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_HOME, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, TF_BUILD, BUILDKITE, DRONE, APPVEYOR, CI, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, TEAMCITY_VERSION, HEROKU_TEST_RUN_ID) — a canonical fingerprinting and sandbox-evasion pattern. The binary reconstructs a URL to `files.catbox.moe` (an anonymous file host commonly abused for malware staging) from split and reversed string fragments so that plain string scans do not reveal the endpoint, and embeds Microsoft-lookalike filenames (EdgeUpdateService.exe, RuntimeBroker-style names) consistent with masquerade staging. The package is nominally a `.env`/config parser but ships only a Windows `.pyd` with dropper and host-fingerprint behavior on import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
